facts.artifact_type: Demeter manual factual extraction; not publisher JSON
facts.intervention: Intensive lifestyle program including diet, physical activity and weight loss; not an isolated UPF intervention
notes: Retain the Figure 2 caption's year-four lifestyle upper limit of 9.4 as printed. The abstract/main text's multiple-imputation analysis gives 8.4; these records do not silently combine the two analyses.
Counts reconcile to the reported rounded percentages. Attrition and repeated-measure covariance preclude treating annual differences as independent causal estimates.
No dose, lag, age modifier or remission hazard is inferred from these observations.
facts.outcome: Partial or complete diabetes remission at the annual visit, without antihyperglycemic medication
facts.population: U.S. Look AHEAD adults recruited at ages 45-76 with overweight/obesity and established type 2 diabetes; includes baseline insulin users
facts.uncertainty: Published 95% confidence intervals; visits are repeated measures, covariance unavailable

limitations: Multicomponent lifestyle trial cannot identify a causal UPF coefficient, its lag, or national age-specific transition rates.
Trial remission is not model healthy state or ordinary prediabetes; diagnosed history and medication status require a separate observation model.
A lagged response is a hazard modifier, not remission prevalence; a direct response-to-prevalence shortcut is challenged, not treated as a valid calibration.
The engine currently leaves T2D absorbing. This known structural limitation remains visible and is not repaired by changing a lag.
Time-varying adherence, eligibility, duration of diabetes, attrition, relapse and changing treatment intensity are unresolved; no fitted optimum lag is reported.
